author: Claude Opus 5.5 (engineering lead, cand-d author)
summary: Family B, cand-d v6 (Q95/Q96). A long head and short tail articulate about a vertical pin with a geared sector; a tail stud with a pivoted lug bar mates with a head cartridge and rigid face teeth. An onboard serial servo winds the sleeve via a torsion spring; a separate positive dog reverses it. A low-lead cam, not the servo or spring, retains a fully locked joint when power is lost. Mechanical flats react servo torque and a cross-pinned collar takes ejection reaction. No magnets, ground-truth docking signal, inter-unit energy transfer or active unloaded holding assumed. The author field preserves the candidate lineage; dossier-v6 names this revision's design authors.
assembly_access: Bench assemble PTFE thrust ring and bronze sleeve onto the H900 housing from the rear. Locate the collar from the actual thrust face and match-ream the collar and housing without the sleeve installed. Clean, refit sleeve and collar, set and flush-finish the two washers and the independent soft keeper rivet through opposed skirt ports; the fitted hollow pin, not the keeper, carries thrust. Check end play before mounting. Fix the driver/spring to the servo spline with a gauged M1.7 rocker screw before there is a housing in its path. The fitted case pads and retained tab locate the servo in its steel cassette with both shell lids open. Set the open datum, insert the preassembled cartridge from the front through the finish-machined window, sliding the open-ended dog and spring pickups together. The front flange bears outside the plate; install the two flush screws into the nut blocks while accessible from above. No press fit over the 7 mm land. Fit the tail stud screws before the controller, through aligned driver ports in the opposite inner wall. Fit hinge plates, ears, sector, pin, joint motor clamp and harness in the open shells; fit boards and cell with edge keepers, then slide in the tapped lid ledges and secure lids. Structural screw threads are in metal. See dossier-v6 for access order and fits; not prototyped.
mount_head: H900 housing flange in front of PA12 end plate, clamped via opposed screws into rear nut blocks. Pitch plane x36.4, common axis y+0.60,z-4.60 mm.
mount_tail: Toothed stud flange fixed by two flush screws from inside the tail end plate into blind metal threads. Pitch plane x-11.6; axis shared with the head.

retention.mechanism: This is a friction wedge only after both crowned lug pads have entered the low-lead lock region. The higher-lead entry, mouth dwell and a jammed or partially seated state are not locks. Axial pull travels through stud rocker/pin, lug pads, bronze cam flanks, front thrust washer, fixed flange, its two steel fasteners and nut blocks to the PA12 shell; opposite-side load enters the tail via the stud flange. Matched face teeth carry torsion and shear by flank reaction; bending loads act through the surviving face rim, pilot and opposed lug reactions. The two-segment body carries these loads through the ears, hinge pin, plates and metal screw attachments. Neither an unpowered servo holding torque nor the continuing presence of spring torque is credited. The spring meters the *closing* torque from a bounded relative angular excursion. The dry/oiled friction cases, upper and lower spring rates, combined external loads, bearing drag and orientation-dependent contact constraints are evaluated in coupler.py.

release.means: Only the head unit powers this release. Reverse input unwinds the closing spring until its separate driver pad contacts the relieved sleeve-skirt wall. Continued motion drives the sleeve toward its open stop. Front PTFE thrust face carries pull-assisted release. During positive ejection the sleeve shifts rearward across its full axial play and bears directly on the cross-pinned H900 collar, then pin, housing and plate. Loaded cases keep the fixed external forces and journal reactions, not a scaling cancellation between motor constants. The spline retains its own hub, not the mating unit. Release requires a serviceable charged head and no responsive tail. The rated torque does NOT cover the one-sided loaded cases. This version cannot declare bounded release under all Q31 loads.

alignment.description: Presented pilot and chamfer into an interrupted guide bore.
alignment.justification: An external quasistatic presentation supplies insertion, not an onboard approach or an invisible fixture holding the assembly during powered closure. The guide channels interrupt the pilot circumference; count only the retained lands, with actual chord clearance at each insertion depth. The guide/rim comparison distinguishes first contact from full seating. No autonomous capture window is inferred from the opening diameter.

alignment.description: Opposed lug guide entries, rocking lug bar and face teeth.
alignment.justification: The slots constrain clocking before tooth contact. The rocker admits unequal axial depths at the two ends; the angled Hirth flanks transmit draw into centring and clocking reactions. The force/stack bounds include tooth standoff and residual tilt, not a snap to a common axis.

alignment.description: Mouth dwell, draw stage and shallow lock stage.
alignment.justification: The operator presents the lugs into the open mouth; the servo takes up a finite angle on the dwell before the rotating flank can pick them up. Only the servo and the series spring then provide draw. An obstructed or off-window start may remain partial; servo position is not an independent indication of tooth seating.

limitations: Gate 1 is paper feasibility only. Q31 starts connected. No autonomous approach, measured capture region or cycle life claimed.
Wedge retention depends on the specified friction regime. Unknown vibration, impact, lubricant, PTFE migration or wear can defeat the self-lock condition.
Spring, dog, keyed mount, precise fits and machined/match-reamed parts are design callouts. Inspect the finished parts. Handbook friction and elastic properties are not component-pair test results.
The regulator and trimmed case are not qualified hardware; verify loaded voltage, torque, current and heating over the operating range. Do not run a blocked servo continuously.
A voltage or internal servo-shaft reading cannot prove latch engagement. No credit for a completed closure after a partial or obstructed motion.
No curvature-holding torque unpowered or five-unit benchmark pass is claimed. Joint angle feedback and the later dynamic articulation benchmark remain open.
Small features, rocker, screw-access fixtures, case clamping without crush, spline profile and end play require bench checks. Part tolerance and assembly acceptance limits are not measurements.
Component boxes are grouping or mass proxies where stated; interlocking internal parts are analysed separately. G5 is the registered three-unit static support calculation at roll zero.
BLE only; no power or wired data exchange between units.
